title: Chapter 1 — JJC
description: DRAFT for approval. Phase 2: opening to the Back Side. Phase 3: first night, fee level, Day 1 fee run, first defaulter. Phase 4 adds the real chase.

cards.title: What you have
cards.text: {money}. A phone on 3%. One bag. One OND certificate in a nylon.

cards.title: What you owe
cards.text: {debt}. Your mother's market women gave it to Double-Double Investment Club because you told them to. Double-Double "migrated to a new server". You cannot go home.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The night bus from Ìlú-Àlàáfíà coughs you out under the flyover. Lagos is already awake. Lagos did not sleep.

beats.speaker: fakeConductor
beats.text: Ehen! Fine boy! Welcome to Lagos! You dey go Oshodi? Na here! Pay your ₦500 for ticket, the bus dey come now now!

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Ticket? For bus stop? Bus never even come.

beats.speaker: fakeConductor
beats.text: Na new law! Government ticket! E dey go up by 6 o'clock. Pay now, you save money. Na investment!

beats.speaker: fakeConductor
beats.text: Quick quick! Before price go up!

options.text: "Oga, show me your ID card first."
Pretend your phone is ringing and walk away

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Hey! Hey! Na who send you to my bus stop?

variants.text: Hey! Ole! Thief! Bring that boy money back before I give you government ticket for your head!
ID card? Hahaha! Ask am again! Ask am which government! Oya go, before I call Baba Ticket!

beats.speaker: fakeConductor
beats.text: Professor! Na joke! I dey do orientation for the new boy!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The "conductor" disappears faster than NEPA light.

variants.text: Your ₦500 comes back to your hand, slightly wet. The "conductor" disappears faster than NEPA light.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: JJC. I fit smell am from Ojota. Fresh from village, your eyes still white like rice. Lagos go redden am small small.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: My name na {name}, sir. I come Lagos to find work.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Work? See am for your front. Danfo stop. Drivers. Money wey dey fly. Agbero, area boy, union boy — call am anything, na work. But na Baba Ticket dey give the work.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: So? You wan meet the Chairman, or you wan stand there dey look like Sunday school teacher?

options.text: "Wetin be your own gain for this one?"

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Good. Hunger dey your eye. Hunger na the first qualification.

variants.text: OND! Hahaha! Why you think say dem dey call me Professor? I get HND. Lagos no dey read certificate, my brother. Lagos dey read pocket.
Ehen! Sense. Ten percent of your first week. Na so Lagos dey run: nobody dey help person for free, and anybody wey talk say e dey help you for free, hold your pocket.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Your phone vibrates. 2%. "MAMA".

beats.speaker: mama
beats.text: {name}! You reach? Iya Bọ́sẹ̀ come house yesterday with three women. Dem sit for our parlour until ten o'clock. Dem drink all our water. Tell me something good.
What do you tell Mama?

options.text: "I don get job already, Mama. Big job."
"I reach, Mama. I go find am. I promise."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The phone dies before she answers. Lagos 1, You 0.

variants.text: You hear her start to cry with joy. Then the phone dies. Somehow that is worse. Lagos 1, You 0.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Motor park dey that side, behind the danfos. Baba Ticket office get green signboard. I go meet you there. No follow strange man again o!

beats.objective: Walk to the motor park office (west, green signboard). Baba Ticket dey wait.

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: Professor. Who be this one? E dey look like person wey come borrow money.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: New boy, Chairman. JJC. Him get strong leg and him no too talk.

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: Strong leg no be qualification. Even goat get four. Ehen. Wetin your name?

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: {name}, sir.

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: Listen, {name}. For Iyana-Wahala, everything na ticket. Danfo stop, ticket. Keke park, ticket. Person sneeze for bus stop... ticket. As the elders say: the rain that beats the farmer... ehn... also needs ticket.

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: I go give you the Back Side. Under the bridge. Where Professor dey sleep.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: I no dey sleep there, Chairman. I dey rest there. Strategically.

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: Every day, you bring ₦15,000 for me. Wetin pass am, na your own. Wetin no reach am...

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Baba Ticket takes a long, slow bite of suya. He does not finish the sentence. He does not need to.

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: You hear me?

options.text: "Yes sir! ₦15,000 every day. You go see work."
"Chairman, Back Side no fit bring ₦15,000. Make e be ₦10,000."
Say nothing. Nod slowly, like Professor does.
options.lockedText: You never study Professor well enough

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: Good. Ambition. I like ambition, as long as e no pass my own.

variants.text: This one get mouth! Ehen. ₦12,000 for this first week. After that we go see whether your mouth fit carry your leg.
Hmm. This one sabi silence. Professor, you don dey teach am already? Good. Silence na the first ticket.

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: Professor, show am the Back Side. And JJC — welcome to Iyana-Wahala. Na here people dey come to become somebody. Or to become nobody. The bus dey go both ways.

beats.objective: Go to the Back Side, under the flyover. Professor dey there.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Back Side. A bus stop sign with no bus stop. A gutter with ambition. Pillars that smell of everything. Your new office.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Rule number one: never count money in front of the person wey give you am. E dey make dem remember say dem get am before.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Rule number two: every driver get story. Learn the story, you go collect the money. Ignore the story, you go collect wahala.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: And my ten percent. No forget. I get good memory for numbers, bad memory for excuses.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Go look around. Learn the place. Mallam Garba get tea, Baba Radio get news, the market get everything. When night reach, come back here. Tomorrow morning, we start work.

beats.objective: Explore Iyana-Wahala. When you're ready to rest, go back to Professor at the Back Side.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Night. Under the bridge, a hundred generators sing a song with no chorus. Professor spreads a flattened carton like a king laying out his bed.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Tomorrow na your first day. Before you sleep, answer me one question. Na the most important question for this work.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: How much you go collect from each danfo?

options.text: "₦300. Make the drivers like me first."
"₦700. Baba Ticket quota no be joke."

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: ₦500. Middle road. Na where most people dey crash, but na also where most people dey reach.

variants.text: ₦300. Soft man. Drivers go love you, and Baba Ticket go ask why your bag light like Sunday offering.
₦700?! Ehen. You wan make enemy before breakfast. Okay. The danfo people get long memory and short temper o.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Your fee fit change any day. But every change, somebody go feel am. Sleep. Mosquito go do the rest.

cards.title: Day 1
cards.text: 6:10 a.m. The Back Side. Your first fee run.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Danfo go stop for this side. Collect from every vehicle wey stop: danfo, keke, okada, even lorry. Smile, collect, move to the next.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Rule number three: the driver wey smile too much na him never pay. Watch Bíọ́dún. Him owe everybody for this junction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Bíọ́dún jumps back into "God's Time Is The Best" and stamps on the accelerator. Passengers scream. One chicken also screams.

variants.text: While you were busy with another driver, "God's Time Is The Best" quietly pulls away. Bíọ́dún waves. He is laughing.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Oga, that driver don run again. You go chase am or you go let am go? Quick quick!

options.text: Let am go, na small money

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Evening go reach, and Baba Ticket go come for him money. Count your bag. Hide small for your sock. Rule number four: sock na the only bank wey no dey close.

beats.objective: Walk around Iyana-Wahala. (Chapter 1 continues in the next update: the real chase, Baba Ticket's collection and the fuel hike.)

beats.title: To be continued
beats.summary: Chapter 1 continues in Phase 4 with the chase, and Phase 5 with energy, Baba Ticket's evening collection and the fuel hike.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You catch the door of "God's Time Is The Best" with one hand and your breath with the other. Passengers clap. One of them is filming.

beats.speaker: biodun
beats.text: Okay! Okay! Na joke I dey joke! Take your ₦500! Haba, you wan kill person for ₦500?

beats.speaker: biodun
beats.text: Na only ₦500 you go collect abi? Abi you wan show me pepper?

options.text: "₦500. Na the fee. Next time no run."
"₦500 plus ₦1,000 for running. Pay or I seize your key."
Give him back the ₦500. "Today na free. Tomorrow no run."

beats.speaker: biodun
beats.text: Hmm. You be correct person. I go remember.

variants.text: ₦1,500?! For one morning? Ehen. I don hear. Lagos small, JJC. Lagos very small.
Free? ... Who send you come this junction? Okay. Okay. I go remember this one. God go bless you, JJC.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: "God's Time Is The Best" turns the corner past the motor park. Bíọ́dún's hand comes out of the window and waves. Slowly. Like a pageant queen.
